profile.reading:
This is a Digital Realty facility at 2055 East Technology Circle, Tempe, AZ, per mapping data. This session's fetch of Digital Realty's Phoenix metro property list did not surface a matching named/coded property at this specific address, so no operator-confirmed square footage is reported here.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building is part of Digital Realty's Phoenix metro footprint, which spans downtown Phoenix and the East Valley cities of Chandler and Tempe, an area that has drawn large hyperscale and colocation investment in recent years partly on the strength of Arizona Public Service and Salt River Project grid capacity. Digital Realty markets its Phoenix properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro alongside Silicon Valley, Northern Virginia, Dallas, Chicago, and New York/New Jersey, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, as core hubs in its global interconnection and colocation platform.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage; the company reports its portfolio metrics by region and metro rather than disclosing per-building IT power ratings for any of its facilities, a pattern consistent across every Digital Realty property researched this session, not specific to this building alone.

reading.body:
This Tempe facility, operated by Digital Realty at 2055 East Technology Circle, is confirmed in location and operator but lacks published power specifications for its individual buildings. The data provided does not include megawatt capacity, critical IT load, or rack count for this site, making it impossible to translate its physical scale into accelerator density or training capability.

Within Arizona's mapped data center footprint of 56 facilities, only 4 have published power figures totaling 512 MW of capacity statewide. This campus ranks fifth among Arizona's published capacity facilities, but without its own published specification, its actual power draw and contribution to that ranking cannot be determined from operator disclosure alone.

The research status is complete for location and operator identity. Whether this facility matters to AI scaling depends on figures not yet published in the operator's spec pages—total power, IT load allocation, and cooling delivery. Until those specifications appear, the site's role in the grid constraint on AI infrastructure remains unmeasured.
